The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

month.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents

threats.headline: OpenSSH flaw allows password authentication bypass in some Linux account configurations
threats.summary: OpenSSH on Linux lacks a workaround for a password authentication bypass when musl libc is used without PAM. For some account configurations, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds.
actions: Apply the vendor's fix or mitigations for OpenBSD OpenSSH: CISA lists it as exploited
who: OpenSSH users on Linux with musl libc without PAM
threats.quote: For some configurations of accounts, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds.

items.title: QA teams can let Codex debug internal staging sites without exposing them
items.connection: Chrome DevTools MCP is becoming a standard agent tool for browser debugging, and OpenAI's secure tunnel connects private or localhost MCP servers to Codex without a public endpoint, so a DevTools server inside the network can serve a cloud agent.
items.context: most staging environments sit behind a VPN and cannot be opened to the internet
chain: Agents can inspect pages, console and network through DevTools MCP.
The tunnel lets a DevTools MCP server running inside the firewall reach Codex.
Agents can reproduce and debug bugs on real internal staging builds, not just public sites.
QA can hand front-end bug tickets to the agent and receive diagnosed reports or fixes, shortening triage.
items.who: QA and front-end teams at enterprises benefit; their engineering orgs would pay through existing OpenAI plans.
items.variable: time from bug report to diagnosis
items.versus: Without the tunnel, teams must either expose staging publicly or keep agents blind to internal apps.
items.smallest_test: Give the agent 10 recent staging bug tickets through the tunnel; succeed if it correctly diagnoses at least 5 with security sign-off on the setup.
items.disconfirm: Security teams refuse the tunnel, or the agent misdiagnoses most staging bugs despite browser access.

items.title: Engineering leads can set a Copilot model routing policy from public scores
items.connection: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is now selectable in Copilot, the Coding Agent Index shows a roughly 30x cost spread among top setups, and Letta scores Hydrogen at 64.4% on memory against Carbon at 71.1%, so there is now enough public data to route work by task length.
items.context: most teams default every developer to one model regardless of task
chain: A fast Flash model is generally available inside Copilot.
The index shows top setups tie at 58 while costs differ about 30x, so price, not score, separates them.
Hydrogen's lower memory score signals it fits short routine tasks better than long multi-session work.
Teams can write a written routing rule: fast model for small edits, stronger model for long-running agent jobs, and track spend per merged PR.
items.who: Engineering managers and platform teams benefit; companies paying Copilot and model bills pay.
items.versus: Doing nothing leaves teams paying top-model prices for routine edits with no evidence it helps.
items.smallest_test: For two weeks, route one team's small tickets to Hydrogen and compare against a control team; succeed if merge rate stays within 5 points while wait time or spend drops.
items.disconfirm: Hydrogen's merge rate on routine tickets falls well below the default model, erasing the savings.

items.title: Open source maintainers can triage agent bug reports by requiring cross-agent agreement
items.connection: Codex Security CLI is spreading as a way to find and fix vulnerabilities, Hermes' plugin verifies candidates with parallel subagents and can reproduce them in a temporary copy, and Patch the Planet connects agent findings with maintainers, so findings confirmed by two separate tools can be sent first.
items.context: maintainers already struggle with low-quality automated bug reports
chain: More teams run agent vulnerability scanners, so report volume to maintainers rises.
A second tool that independently reproduces a finding filters out many false alarms.
Coordination programs can prioritize cross-confirmed findings for disclosure.
Maintainer time shifts from rejecting noise to fixing real bugs, and coordinators can set a reproduction bar for submissions.
items.who: Open source maintainers and foundations benefit; foundations, coordination programs and companies that depend on the code would fund it.
items.versus: Forwarding raw scanner output overloads maintainers, while doing nothing leaves agent-found bugs undisclosed.
items.smallest_test: Run both tools on 5 popular repos with past CVEs; succeed if cross-confirmed findings have at least twice the true-positive rate of single-tool findings.
items.disconfirm: The two tools agree almost never, or agreed findings are no more accurate than single-tool ones.

items.title: Security consultancies can sell bug-hunting agent evals anchored to an open baseline
items.connection: An open-weight model just cleared 1% on the hard SWE-sweep bug-finding benchmark, Anthropic published guidance on designing, running and reporting evaluations, and the harness leaderboard shows demand for comparing harnesses, which together give a method and a floor for client-specific evals.
items.context: firms buying AI security tools lack independent ways to measure them
chain: A public open-weight baseline for real bug finding now exists, even if low.
Anthropic's guidance gives a reference for how to design and report evals credibly.
Consultants can run the open baseline and vendor tools on a client's own seeded bugs, comparing harnesses as well as models.
Clients get procurement evidence, and vendors face pressure to publish comparable results.
items.who: CISOs and procurement teams benefit; enterprises buying agent security tools would pay consultancies.
items.variable: real bugs found per review hour
items.versus: Vendor claims and GitHub stars do not show detection accuracy on a client's own code.
items.smallest_test: Seed 20 known bugs in a client-like repo and score the open baseline plus two commercial tools with a written protocol; succeed if results separate tools by a clear margin a client would act on.
items.disconfirm: All tools score near zero on seeded bugs, so the eval cannot distinguish options.

items.title: Legacy front-end modernization agents can pass a design review and hard gates first
items.connection: On 2026-11-13 Magpie suggested a proactive repo agent modernize legacy front ends using Chrome's guidance and DevTools MCP; today Google's open-source design review plugin adds a structured review before code, and build-failing WCAG 2.2 and design-token gates catch PRs that ignore the guidance, which targets the idea's main failure.
items.context: public sector sites face accessibility rules and large legacy code bases
chain: The earlier loop failed when PRs ignored guidance or broke pages.
A design review plugin forces the agent to state and get review on its plan before editing.
50 build-failing gates reject PRs that miss accessibility or design rules before a human sees them.
Agencies can run modernization as a steady backlog with reviewers only seeing PRs that already passed.
items.who: Government and university web teams benefit; their digital service budgets or contracted agencies would pay.
items.variable: share of agent PRs merged without rework
items.versus: The idea without review and gates leaves humans to catch every guidance miss by hand.
items.smallest_test: Run the loop with and without design review plus gates on one legacy site; succeed if the gated loop has a clearly higher merge rate.
items.disconfirm: Gated PRs are merged no more often than ungated ones, or the gates block nearly every PR.

kept.reason: Windsurf's session-level MCP server controls let users toggle and re-authenticate an MCP server like Chrome DevTools MCP during agent work.
It connects private or localhost MCP servers like Chrome DevTools MCP to ChatGPT, Codex, the Responses API and AgentKit without exposing a public endpoint.
Gentle AI configures coding agents with chosen MCP servers, giving a repeatable way to set up browser debugging across agents.
Vulnerability coordination connects agent discoveries with maintainers, researchers and incident responders.
GPT-6 Cyber is an OpenAI model built to find and fix vulnerabilities within authorized scope, the kind of model a security CLI for finding and fixing flaws would use.
SkillSpector scans Codex and MCP skills for injection and supply-chain risks before install, covering the agent's own tooling while the CLI covers the code.
The self-hosted call center packages telephony and human handoff around realtime voice models, a deployment step that an API with voice, search and files does not cover.
LiveKit's approach to voice agents that keep working through interruptions adds a handling step the DeepSeek voice API description does not mention.
DeepSeek Harness has a documented Cordis plugin system, a path for builders to wrap the new search, files and voice features as agent plugins.
ForgeKernel's open harness has an agent optimize GPU kernels and produced a faster fused prefill kernel, which could tune the CUDA engine's long-context prefill.
Modal's library covers long-context RL and fine-tuning on on-demand clusters, the training step before a lean engine serves the model.
The Hermes plugin reviews a repository for security bugs with verification by subagents, covering a security step alongside design review.
Build-failing accessibility and design-token gates add enforceable implementation checks after agent design and review.
The cross-tool marketplace lets the same agent plugins be reused across seven coding agent tools, a route to using the design review plugin on mixed tooling.
ExecuTorch WebGPU runs exported PyTorch models locally in Chrome, so agents guided by current web best practices could build front ends that also run models client side.
The proactive repository agent supplies an issue-to-PR workflow in which to apply the web guidance.
AutoRLBench tests agents on diagnosing real failed RL runs, a second real-failure yardstick next to the bug-finding baseline.
MaxxBench spreads apart models that tie on a headline coding score by applying small task edits, which could help separate the two models tied at 58.
Tracking possible Opus changes adds ongoing monitoring after a point-in-time coding-agent comparison.
Claude Fable 5.2 is available in GitHub Copilot for multistep coding tasks, so teams can try one of the index's tied leaders in an existing workflow.
